world.headline: Iranian death toll from the latest US strikes rises to 18 as Trump threatens more
world.body: Iran says 18 people were killed and at least 108 wounded in the wave of US strikes on its southern coast, including five killed at a wedding party in Kuhestak in Sirik county, Hormozgan province. Iran's foreign ministry called the wedding strike a war crime; US Central Command said it was conducting strikes in the vicinity and would investigate reports of civilian casualties. Trump told reporters at the White House it was a very heavy attack and that the US is prepared to do another one anytime we want, after hitting rebuilt radar sites along the Strait of Hormuz.

world.headline: Nepal flood death toll passes 1,000 with 3,916 still missing
world.body: Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority now counts at least 1,010 dead, 1,473 injured and 3,916 missing after the Nepal-China flash floods, with 11,814 people rescued. Citizens of 38 countries are among the missing, and roughly 747 people, including some 583 tourists, are unaccounted for in Rasuwa district on the Tibet border. Crews are still trying to reach workers feared trapped in mud-filled hydropower tunnels.

world.headline: Brent holds near $95 a barrel as the Hormuz exchange keeps a risk premium in place
world.body: Brent crude traded around $94.86 a barrel on 2 September, up about 13% over the past month and roughly 40% higher than a year ago. The move follows the renewed US strikes on Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz and Trump's warning of a far larger response to any Iranian retaliation. Sustained crude above $90 feeds directly into import bills and inflation for oil-importing economies.

world.headline: Germany blames Russia for the attempted drone attack on Leipzig-Halle airport
world.body: Berlin says an explosive-laden drone that fell beside a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig-Halle airport on 4 August and was defused by a bomb squad was operated on behalf of Russian state entities. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called it part of a known pattern of Russian hybrid operations; Germany summoned Moscow's ambassador and ordered the closure of the Russian consulate general in Bonn and the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin. Putin rejected the accusation, saying Berlin had fabricated the evidence.

world.headline: Russia fires 174 drones and four missiles at Ukraine overnight, with hits at 16 locations
world.body: Ukraine's air force says it downed or jammed 141 of the 174 incoming weapons launched overnight into 2 September, which included two Iskander-M ballistic missiles from occupied Crimea, two Kh-59/69 guided missiles over the Black Sea, and Shahed-type, Banderol and Gerbera drones. Strikes registered at 16 locations; a drone hit a six-storey residential building in Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi district and seven people were injured in the capital. Power outages were reported across five regions, with Odesa the worst affected.

world.headline: OpenAI says its Astra model is the first to cross its Critical cybersecurity threshold
world.body: OpenAI announced that Astra meets the Critical cybersecurity capability tier under its Preparedness Framework, meaning that with tools and access it can find previously unknown flaws and build working exploits across hardened systems without step-by-step human direction. The company reported a perfect score on ExploitBench and said Astra is markedly more capable and more token-efficient than GPT-5.6 Sol. Access to the most advanced cyber capabilities will initially be limited to a small group of testers, with defensive use expanded later.

world.headline: Justice Department backs OpenAI's fair-use defence in the New York Times case
world.body: The Trump administration filed a statement of interest with Judge Sidney Stein in the Southern District of New York arguing that training large language models on copyrighted text is fair use. It is the federal government's first formal intervention in the wave of copyright suits brought against AI developers by authors, publishers, music labels and news organisations, and frames the question as one of scientific advancement, economic development and national security. The Times, which sued OpenAI and Microsoft in late 2023, criticised the filing.

world.headline: World Food Programme halves food assistance in the occupied West Bank
world.body: WFP said a funding shortfall forces it to cut the number of people it feeds in the West Bank from 400,000 to 200,000 from September. The agency needs an additional $386 million over the next six months to reach an estimated two million food-insecure people across Gaza and the West Bank, and warned further cuts in Gaza are unavoidable without new money. Its latest analysis found 76% of West Bank households have seen a significant fall in income and a third cannot afford a nutritious diet.

world.headline: Jefferson Lab physicists hunting one exotic particle find two unexpected structures
world.body: Researchers at Jefferson Lab searching the strange quark sector for a single predicted particle instead found evidence of two distinct structures that may belong to the XYZ family, exotic states that do not fit neatly into the conventional quark model. It is the first time such signals have been produced by a beam of high-energy photons striking a proton target. The result gives theorists a fresh handle on how the strong force binds matter at short range.

world.headline: Alcaraz wins on his return at the US Open as Tsitsipas knocks out the 10th seed
world.body: Carlos Alcaraz, playing his first singles match in 139 days, beat Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the first round at Flushing Meadows, while defending champion Aryna Sabalenka opened with a straight-sets win over Camila Osorio. The day's biggest upset came from Stefanos Tsitsipas, who beat Cincinnati champion and 10th seed Arthur Fils 4-6, 7-6(3), 6-1, 6-4. Tsitsipas next faces South Africa's Lloyd Harris.

india.headline: 288 Indians still missing in the Nepal floods as Delhi sends tunnel rescue specialists
india.body: Indians make up the largest group of foreign nationals unaccounted for after the Nepal-China floods, with 288 still missing, up from the 275 figure reported earlier this week. India has flown in 18 army officers trained in tunnel rescue and six teams of forensic experts for DNA-based identification, alongside four tranches of relief including generators, water purification tablets, tents and medicine. Among the missing is Laxminath Gopisetty, chief executive of Infosys Public Services, who was travelling with a group of 11.

india.headline: August GST collections rise 14.8% to Rs 1.99 lakh crore
india.body: Gross GST revenue reached Rs 1,99,853 crore in August, up from about Rs 1.74 lakh crore a year earlier, on government data released this week. Import IGST jumped 29% to Rs 62,604 crore while domestic collections grew 9.3% to about Rs 1.37 lakh crore; net revenue rose a slower 8.3% to Rs 1.68 lakh crore because refunds climbed 68%. Cumulative gross collections for April to August stand at Rs 10.43 lakh crore, 11% higher than the same period last year.

india.headline: Sensex falls a third straight session as crude and bond yields bite
india.body: The Sensex closed 374 points lower at 76,570 on Tuesday, extending losses to a third session as the spike in oil prices revived inflation worries and rising bond yields dented risk appetite. Auto and IT stocks were the biggest drags. With Brent holding near $95, the pressure on the import bill and on margins for oil-linked sectors is the market's dominant near-term concern.

india.headline: Supreme Court invokes Article 142 to quash FIRs against NEET-UG protesters
india.body: A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant ordered that FIRs registered against students who protested the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak between 20 and 25 July be closed, using the court's Article 142 power to do complete justice. The order covers Delhi, Assam, West Bengal and Bihar, and Delhi Police alone had registered 13 FIRs over demonstrations at Jantar Mantar. Police may still proceed against 2,873 people identified as having serious criminal antecedents, and the Solicitor General assured the court no fresh FIRs would be filed over that period.

india.headline: FSSAI proposes red hexagonal warning labels on packaged food high in fat, sugar or salt
india.body: In a compliance affidavit filed before the Supreme Court in a public interest case, the food regulator proposed front-of-pack warning labels using a red hexagon and declarations such as High Fat, High Sugar, High Salt and Highly Sweetened Beverage. The symbol would use a font larger than that of the standard nutrition panel so shoppers can identify high-risk products at a glance. The Supreme Court is due to review the framework on 10 September.

india.headline: Reliance-backed Digital Connexion commits $11 billion to a 1 GW data centre hub in Visakhapatnam
india.body: Digital Connexion, a joint venture of Reliance Industries, Brookfield Infrastructure and Digital Realty, signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board to invest about $11 billion by 2030 building 1 gigawatt of AI-native data centre capacity across 400 acres. The venture, formed in December 2023, already runs a campus in Chennai and is building a 40 MW facility in Mumbai. It adds to a run of large commitments in India, including Google's $15 billion AI hub and Amazon's $12.7 billion cloud plan.

india.headline: NOTAM points to a 2,995 km missile test off the Odisha coast this week
india.body: India has issued a Notice to Air Missions covering a 2,995 km corridor over the Indian Ocean for a launch window of 2 to 3 September, with the test expected from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, the DRDO and Strategic Forces Command range off Odisha. The range has revived talk of an Agni-6, though the declared distance points more plausibly to an Agni-3 or Agni-4 class system. No official confirmation of the payload has been issued.

india.headline: GSLV-F17 set to lift EOS-05 from Sriharikota at 2.55 am on Friday
india.body: ISRO's 19th GSLV flight will place the 2,367 kg EOS-05 Earth observation satellite into a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit from the second launch pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre on 4 September, with live coverage from 2.25 am. The rocket was rolled from the vehicle assembly building to the umbilical tower on 28 August. EOS-05 will be India's first imaging satellite to work from geostationary orbit, replacing GISAT-1A, which was lost in a launch failure in 2021.

india.headline: IMD issues rain alerts across 19 states with flash flood risk in Jharkhand
india.body: The weather office has warned of heavy to very heavy rain on 3 September across Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and parts of the northeast, with gusts up to 65 km/h and thunderstorm warnings. Flash flooding is flagged for Jharkhand and isolated extremely heavy rain for east Madhya Pradesh. Landslide risk is rated moderate to high across Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.

india.headline: India play Hong Kong China today at the Women's Asia Cup before Friday's Pakistan tie
india.body: Harmanpreet Kaur's side, who opened with a 94-run win over Thailand, face Hong Kong China in Dubai on 3 September in their second Group A match. India, seven-time champions and the most successful side in the tournament's history, meet Pakistan on 5 September. The T20 tournament runs at the Dubai International Stadium until 13 September.
